Modern.tagline: Modern furniture in the watershed year.
Modern.brandNameRationale: 1948 was the watershed year of American modernism — Charles Eames's LCW chair, Eero Saarinen's Womb Chair, and the founding generation of the Knoll Planning Unit. The year is public-domain, the anchor is design-historical, and 'Form' names what modernism gave the living room: organic shape, clear function.
Modern.industrySummary: Modern furniture has split between fast-fashion imports and a small considered-modern cohort. The opening is for a studio that anchors on the specific historical moment when organic modernism entered the home, and builds a small permanent catalog from that vocabulary.
Modern.competitorLandscape: Design Within Reach (dwr.com) holds the considered-modern retail position. Blu Dot (bludot.com) sits in the design-led DTC tier. HAY (hay.com) is the Danish modern peer. We sit closer to Blu Dot in scale with sharper historical grounding.
Modern.positioningStatement: A modern furniture studio whose forms are rooted in the 1948 organic-modern moment.

targetAudience.primary: 32 to 55. Owns one home, furnishing it slowly. Knows the difference between Saarinen and Eames. Buys one piece every two years and keeps it.
behaviors: Researches the designer before the purchase
Will pay 3x for the right chair

dos: Name the joinery and the wood
Show the chair, not the room

Modern.logoDirection: A wordmark — Form 1948 set in a precise mid-century grotesk, with the year tucked beneath the word. A small geometric mark of a curved chair-shell silhouette serves as the hangtag stamp.

typography.primary: Akzidenz-Grotesk for the wordmark and headlines
typography.secondary: Akzidenz-Grotesk for body and product cards
typography.rationale: One family across the system. The face was contemporary to the 1948 forms.

Luxury.brandNameRationale: André-Charles Boulle (1642–1732) was Louis XIV's cabinetmaker who pioneered brass-and-tortoiseshell marquetry ('Boulle work'). The technique and the maker are public-domain historical references. Maison closes the brand as a French house.
Luxury.industrySummary: Luxury furniture at the couture tier is dominated by 20th-century maisons. The opening is for a small house reviving 17th-century royal marquetry for collectors who commission rather than browse.
Luxury.competitorLandscape: Linley (davidlinley.com) holds the British bespoke-luxury slot. Maison Jansen (historically) is the institutional reference. Pierre Yovanovitch (pierreyovanovitch.com) is the modern-luxury peer. We sit closer to Linley in posture with a sharper Boulle-marquetry specialty.
Luxury.positioningStatement: A couture cabinetry house reviving royal Boulle marquetry for collectors of one-off pieces.

targetAudience.primary: 55 to 80. Multi-generational collector. Owns at least one piece by a Versailles-tradition ébéniste. Commissions rather than buys.
behaviors: Travels to Paris for the atelier visit
Pays in installments over two years

dos: Speak in the language of marquetry and ormolu

Luxury.logoDirection: A serif wordmark — Boulle Maison set in a classical French roman with a small embossed mark depicting the Boulle marquetry pattern. The mark appears on commission certificates and the atelier door.

typography.primary: Didot for the wordmark and certificates
typography.secondary: Adobe Garamond for body and commission documents
typography.rationale: Didot carries the French royal display tradition. Garamond keeps the documentation warm.

Minimal.brandNameRationale: Sashimono is the Japanese tradition of furniture assembled entirely with hidden joinery — no nails, no glue. The technique is documented from the Edo period (1603–1868). The word is the technique; the brand is the practice.
Minimal.industrySummary: Minimal furniture has converged on Scandinavian visual cues. The opening underneath is the Japanese sashimono tradition — a different vocabulary of restraint, organized around the joint rather than the surface.
Minimal.competitorLandscape: Maruni (maruni.com) holds the Japanese-modern peer slot. Time & Style (timeandstyle.com) is the Japanese-luxury reference. Karimoku (karimoku-newstandard.jp) sits in the considered-Japanese position. We sit closer to Time & Style with a sashimono specialty.
Minimal.positioningStatement: Minimal furniture in the Japanese nail-less joinery tradition.

targetAudience.primary: 30 to 55. Owns a small home. Reads Kinfolk and Real Cities. Will wait six months for the right piece.
behaviors: Studies the joint, not the surface
Buys one piece every three years

donts: Use the word minimal as marketing
Photograph the piece in styled rooms

Minimal.logoDirection: A wordmark — Sashimono set in a calm humanist sans with a small kerf-mark (a single fine line) above the word. The kerf-mark alone is the favicon.

typography.primary: Neue Haas Grotesk for the wordmark and body
typography.rationale: One face. The brand is the joint, not the type.

Corporate.tagline: Contract-grade furniture for the spec sheet.
Corporate.brandNameRationale: Contract furniture is the industry term for commercial-grade specification work (distinct from residential). Hall evokes the trade-show floor (NeoCon, since 1969). The two words name the buyer and the venue.
Corporate.industrySummary: Contract furniture is a serious B2B category. The buyers are architects, FF&E consultants, and corporate facilities directors. The vendors compete on code compliance, lead time, and durability across thousands of seats.
Corporate.competitorLandscape: Steelcase (steelcase.com) is the institutional benchmark. Haworth (haworth.com) holds the multi-line peer slot. Andreu World (andreuworld.com) is the Spanish design-led peer. We sit smaller and more design-led than Steelcase, more reliable than the boutiques.
Corporate.positioningStatement: Contract furniture for architects and FF&E consultants — durable, code-compliant, spec-ready.

targetAudience.primary: 45 to 60. Architects, FF&E consultants, corporate facilities VPs. Manage multi-million-dollar fit-outs.
behaviors: Requests spec sheets and BIM models first

Corporate.logoDirection: A wordmark with a small geometric mark — a stylized plan-view chair icon to the left. CONTRACT HALL set in a tight modern grotesk, suitable for spec books, name badges, and trade-show banners.

typography.primary: Inter for marketing and B2B materials
typography.secondary: Source Serif Pro for printed spec books and RFPs
typography.rationale: Inter scales clean across digital. The serif handles printed FF&E documentation.

Creative.brandNameRationale: Achille Castiglioni (1918–2002) was a Milanese designer whose Mezzadro tractor-seat stool (1957) and Arco floor lamp pioneered the readymade-as-furniture school. The surname is the designer's, public-domain as historical reference, and 'Lab' signals the experimental posture.
Creative.industrySummary: Creative furniture has been crowded with maximalist postmodernism. The opening is for a studio working in the Castiglioni readymade tradition — found industrial objects elevated into furniture.
Creative.competitorLandscape: Moooi (moooi.com) holds the conceptual-creative slot. Established & Sons (establishedandsons.com) sits in the design-edition tier. Magis (magisdesign.com) plays the Italian-creative peer. We sit closer to Magis with a sharper readymade specialty.
Creative.positioningStatement: A witty, readymade-driven creative furniture lab in the Castiglioni tradition.

targetAudience.primary: 30 to 50. Design-literate buyer. Owns at least one piece of Italian-design history. Reads Domus and Disegno. Buys for the conversation.

dos: Show the piece in a working room

Creative.logoDirection: A wordmark — Castiglioni Lab set in a punchy Italian sans with a small readymade icon (a stylized industrial bolt) as the mark. The bolt alone is the favicon.

typography.primary: PP Mori for the wordmark and headlines
typography.secondary: GT Sectra for product descriptions and editorial
typography.rationale: Mori carries the wit. Sectra makes the catalog copy feel like a small design magazine.
